overview.headline: Mach number links flight speed to sound speed and controls air density changes

keyPoints.point: Aircraft at low speed show constant air density with little compression effect
keyPoints.quote: If the aircraft passes at a low speed, typically less than 250 mph, it is observed that the density of the air remains constant.

keyPoints.point: Mach number is defined as ratio of aircraft speed to speed of sound in gas
keyPoints.quote: The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

keyPoints.point: Supersonic and hypersonic flows show density changes faster than velocity changes by square of Mach number
keyPoints.quote: For supersonic and hypersonic flows, the density changes faster than the velocity changes by a factor equal to the square of the Mach number.

keyPoints.point: Subsonic conditions have Mach number very small so square of Mach number is very small
keyPoints.quote: For low speed, or subsonic conditions, the Mach number is less than one, M < 1, and the square of the Mach number is very small.

keyTerms.gloss: ratio of aircraft speed to speed of sound used to gauge compressibility
keyTerms.quote: The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

keyTerms.gloss: speed at which small disturbances travel through gas isentropically
keyTerms.quote: Near and beyond the speed of sound, about 330 m/s or 760 mph at sea level

keyTerms.gloss: effect where air density changes as flow is compressed at higher speed
keyTerms.quote: This compressibility effect alters the amount of resulting force on the aircraft since the aerodynamic force depends on the air density.

keyTerms.gloss: transmission with constant entropy and no heat exchange
keyTerms.quote: small disturbances in the flow are transmitted to other locations isentropically or with constant entropy

keyTerms.gloss: sharp disturbances that create abrupt changes in lift and drag downstream
keyTerms.quote: Sharp disturbances generate shock waves that affect both the lift and drag of the aircraft and the flow conditions downstream of the shock wave.
